THE CORE IDEA

runs.text: In the short run, at least one input is fixed, so output changes as additional units of a variable input are employed. Input flexibility is the production-side basis for distinguishing fixed and variable cost. The same arithmetic relationship governs MP versus AP and MC versus AVC or ATC.

WORKED EXAMPLE: DIMINISHING MARGINAL PRODUCT

runs.text: Horizontal axis: Workers; vertical axis: Total output. The TP line connects output 0 with no workers, about 8 with 1, 20 with 2, 34 with 3, 46 with 4, 56 with 5, 64 with 6, 70 with 7 and 74 with 8 workers. Output rises throughout; the line becomes flatter after the third worker. Values without printed point labels are approximate readings from the scale.

runs.text: Total product rises from 34 units with three workers to 46 with four, so the fourth worker's marginal product is 12. The fifth worker raises output from 46 to 56, giving marginal product of 10. Output still increases, but the smaller addition shows diminishing marginal product.
